title: DNA: Base Pairs and Replication
text: DNA consists of two polynucleotide strands forming a double helix, held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs: adenine (A) pairs with thymine (T), and guanine (G) pairs with cytosine (C). This base-pairing specificity is fundamental to DNA replication, where each strand serves as a template for synthesis of a new complementary strand. DNA replication is catalyzed by DNA polymerase and occurs in the 5' to 3' direction. The human genome contains approximately 3 billion base pairs distributed across 23 pairs of chromosomes in the cell nucleus. Errors in replication (mutations) can lead to genetic diseases or cancer.
